name: Elhanan
title: The Hero Who Struck Down a Giant
summary: Elhanan was a brave warrior in King David's army, known for killing a Philistine giant. There are two references to an Elhanan in the Bible: one who killed Goliath from Gath (2 Samuel 21:19) and one who killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath (1 Chronicles 20:5). These references have been the subject of much discussion among biblical scholars regarding their relationship to David's battle with Goliath.

keyEvents.title: Elhanan Kills a Philistine Giant
keyEvents.description: In a battle against the Philistines at Gob, Elhanan son of Jaare-Oregim from Bethlehem killed a giant. This event is recorded in 2 Samuel 21:19 and has been widely discussed in relation to David's fight with Goliath.

keyEvents.title: The Parallel Account in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: In 1 Chronicles 20:5, Elhanan son of Jair is identified as the one who killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath from Gath. This version harmonizes the account with David's famous battle against Goliath.

keyEvents.title: Context: Battles Against Philistine Giants
keyEvents.description: Elhanan is mentioned as part of a series of battles between David's men and Philistine giants, where several of David's heroes defeated warriors from the Rephaim clan.

keyEvents.title: Elhanan Among David's Heroes
keyEvents.description: An Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem is listed among David's thirty mighty men, showing his prominent position among David's most trusted warriors.

keyEvents.title: Parallel list of David's heroes in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem is also mentioned in the parallel list of David's heroes in 1 Chronicles, confirming his position as one of David's foremost warriors.
